issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Appendix B, Type Operators / As: as<T>(argument Any) returns null when the argument is not of the specified runtime type.
issues.evidence: Fresh HISTORIAN probe translated primitive as-casts as pass-through SQL: `5 as String` -> `5`, `'5' as Integer` -> `'5'`, `true as Integer` -> `TRUE`; both native-loaded and forced Python DuckDB connections returned non-null original values instead of null.
issues.root_cause: The CQL translator handled binary `as` by returning the left operand unchanged for all non-Quantity targets, so primitive type assertions behaved like pass-through expressions rather than returning null when runtime types did not match.
issues.resolution: Added primitive-target handling for binary `as`: exact matching primitive literals pass through, mismatched primitive literals lower to SQL NULL, `as Any` preserves input, known conversion-function outputs are statically checked, and dynamic FHIR/measure values use lexical guards plus TRY_CAST so matching runtime primitives become typed SQL values while mismatches return NULL.
